Welcome to the documentation for the **Colorado Pollen Detection** project. This pipeline is designed to handle high-resolution `.czi` (Zeiss) microscopy scans, segment individual pollen grains, and classify them by species using state-of-the-art YOLOv11 models.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Segmentation-Based**: All labeling in this project is performed as **Instance Segmentation** (polygons), not just bounding boxes. This allows for precise measurements of pollen area and diameter.

## 🚀 Key Features

- **High-Resolution Tiling**: Effortlessly process scans larger than 20,000 pixels by decomposing them into manageable training tiles.
- **Max-Z Projection**: Automated MIP reduction to consolidate focus levels without losing detail.
- **Pseudo-Labelling**: Leverages existing models to auto-annotate new datasets, drastically reducing manual effort.
- **Cloud Scale**: Support for Kubernetes-based distributed ingestion on CESNET.

## 📦 Data Storage Policy

To keep the repository lightweight and efficient, large datasets and model weights are **not** stored on GitHub. Instead, they are synchronized with the **CESNET S3 (S3.cl4.du.cesnet.cz)** storage.

- **Source Scans**: Stored in `s3://bucket/Ostatni/Colorado_pollen/Species/`
- **YOLO Datasets**: Stored in `s3://bucket/Ostatni/Colorado_pollen_detection/staging_area/`
- **Models**: Stored in `s3://bucket/Ostatni/Colorado_pollen_detection/trained_models/`

## 📖 Get Started

Check the following sections to get up and running:

- [Ingestion Tutorial](tutorials/ingestion.qmd): How to convert your first .czi folder.
- **Training**: Set up GPU training using `src/train_pollen.py`.
- **Pseudo-Labeling**: Auto-annotate tiles using `src/pseudo_label.py`.
